executiveSummary: Strong problem signal from solo operators and clear willingness-to-pay for an AI-first inbox-driven CRM, but adoption friction (BYOK + inbox access) and lack of Outlook coverage hold the composite below the PROCEED threshold. Pivot: anchor on solo consultants on Google Workspace, lead with 'your tenant, your key' trust messaging.

scores.explanation: Multiple personas describe abandoning prior CRMs within 30 days; urgent admin pain.
Lost-revenue triggers cited but no contractual deadline.
Maya signals <$30/mo ceiling; agency owner accepts $79 team tier.
'Zero forms' wedge is genuinely novel vs HubSpot/Salesforce.
Buy with conditions; trust/data-residency objection unresolved.
Solo consultants on Google Workspace is a clear wedge; Outlook 25% gap.
BYOK + inbox read permission is a high-trust posture.
Outlook gap + trust messaging required before scaling.

evidence.quote: Manual CRM data entry kills 30 minutes a day; I abandoned the last 3 CRMs.
Lost a $12k retainer because I forgot to follow up.
Buy with conditions: BYOK trust story must be first-class.

counterSignals.quote: I don't trust an LLM to read my inbox even if it stays in my tenant.
No SOC2 yet — blocks enterprise pilots.

assumptions.text: Solo operators will trust an LLM with inbox read access if the key stays in their tenant.
assumptions.validationStrategy: 5 design partners, written BYOK acceptance before scaffolding.

assumptions.text: Pricing at <$30/mo solo / $79 team removes the 'do I need this?' objection.
assumptions.validationStrategy: Smoke-test landing page with the two prices; measure click-through to checkout.

assumptions.text: Gmail + Calendar integration covers ≥80% of the wedge market.
assumptions.validationStrategy: Survey 50 design-partner prospects on email platform.

risks.risk: BYOK + inbox-read posture suppresses trial-to-paid conversion.
risks.mitigation: Lead with 'your tenant, your key' on landing page; offer on-device summarisation tier.

risks.risk: HubSpot Free is sticky and free — incumbent retention is the real moat.
risks.mitigation: Position against effort, not features. '0 fields to fill' as the headline.

risks.risk: Outlook gap excludes ~25% of SMB in year 1.
risks.mitigation: Ship Outlook integration by month 6; gate enterprise outreach until then.

nextSteps.rationale: Validates the riskiest assumption before scaffolding.

nextSteps.title: Smoke-test landing page at $29 solo / $79 team
nextSteps.rationale: Quantifies willingness-to-pay before committing engineering effort.

Email-platform survey across 50 prospects (Gmail vs Outlook vs other)

nextSteps.rationale: Confirms differentiation is durable and not a feature war.

decisionRationale: Composite score 62 < PROCEED threshold (68): strong problem but trust/coverage gaps.
Adoption friction 65 with willingness-to-pay 58 — pivot required to anchor on trust-tolerant Google-Workspace solos.
Buying-committee consensus is 'buy with conditions', not 'buy outright' → unresolved objections must be retired before PROCEED.
Differentiation 72 and problem 78 are too strong to KILL: pivot is the rational stance.
